title: Punjab Sets May 26 Date for 105-Body Civic Polls
excerpt: State Election Commissioner Raj Kamal Chaudhury announces sweeping urban local body elections across eight municipal corporations and 76 councils.
body:
Punjab's State Election Commissioner Raj Kamal Chaudhury announced on May 11 that the state will hold urban local body elections on May 26, putting over 3.6 million voters across 105 municipal bodies on a tight two-week countdown.

**What the polls cover:**
The elections span 105 local bodies in total — eight municipal corporations, 76 municipal councils, and 21 Nagar Panchayats — covering 2,019 wards, making it one of the largest civic exercises in the state. Chaudhury confirmed elections for the corporations of Mohali, Bathinda, Abohar, Barnala, Kapurthala, Moga, Batala, and Pathankot.

**How the schedule runs:**
Nomination filing opens May 13 and closes May 16, scrutiny of papers takes place May 18, and polling runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on May 26, with ballots counted on May 29 at designated counting centres. About 36,000 election personnel and 35,500 police personnel will be deployed on election duty, with senior officers appointed in each district as observers. The Model Code of Conduct came into immediate effect in all scheduled areas the moment the announcement was made.

**Why this matters for AAP:**
These polls serve as a critical mid-term report card for Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's AAP government, which swept the 2022 state assembly elections on promises of clean governance and development. The civic bodies elected on May 26 are expected to play a key role in local governance and development planning. The State Election Commission ordered videography of the entire nomination filing process to ensure transparency.

**What to watch next:**
Nomination filings begin May 13, and the withdrawal deadline of May 19 will reveal which parties field serious candidates — watch closely for how AAP, Congress, and the BJP position themselves in key urban centres like Mohali and Pathankot.
